assessments.reasoning: The 20021204211359 capture of OSI’s licenses/osl.php matches the claimed HTML digest. Under the v. 1.1 heading, the body prescribes “Licensed under the Open Software License version 1.1” immediately following the copyright notice and then sets out the grant.
The pinned Index scope includes historical editions whose controlling publication supplies identifiable text and a grant. The archived 1.1 article supplies both.

Although the thread subject mentions AFL, Rosen expressly includes OSL before 3.0 in the quoted removal request. Smith’s suggestion to retain superseded versions for legacy uses explains the proposed local treatment of 1.1.

challenge.method: Distinguished the article from the generic osl.php URL, sidebar approval-process link, website footer and “1.0 vs 1.1 Diff” link. Checked the historical classification against the correspondence and SPDX flags.
challenge.results: The article heading, flat-text link and application notice all identify 1.1. The approval-process link and Rosen’s recollection do not document an edition-specific board action. SPDX records both isOsiApproved=false and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false.

limitations: The historical classification preserves a reference for legacy use. Neither continued rights in a particular work nor their invalidation follows from the classification.
reasoning: The archived OSI page identifies version 1.1 inside the license itself. Its grant and edition meet the Index’s admission criterion, and 1.1 falls within Rosen’s express pre-3.0 chronology.
